subject: Stakeholder handshake: evaluation metrics, ops ownership, and cost limits
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Juan Ramirez <juan@stellarlex.com>, Priya Shah <priya@stellarlex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder handshake: evaluation metrics, ops ownership, and cost limits

Thanks again for the conversation this morning — good alignment overall. The purpose of this thread is to capture the agreed evaluation plan, success criteria, owners, and immediate next steps so we have a single source of truth heading into the PoC. Please call out anything you disagree with.

High-level scope (confirmed on call)
- Workload: conversational retrieval + short-form generation for customer support (see attached evaluation_workload.csv).
- Duration: 6-week PoC with a progressive set of tests (smoke -> scale -> stability).

Success criteria (proposed / agreed subject to confirmation)
1) Latency: p95 inference latency < 250 ms for single-turn gen on typical request mix.
2) Throughput: sustain 200 QPS with 95th percentile latency SLO intact during scale test window.
3) Unit cost: average cost per token <= $0.0009 during the steady-state run (noting bundling for embeddings separate).
4) Quality: >= 92% pass rate on your labeled evaluation set (we'll run blind evaluations against the golden set in week 4).
5) Reliability: 99.5% availability during business hours (weekdays 9–6 PT) for the dedicated test window.

Owners and roles
- Redwood (technical lead): Ben Carter — infra, telemetry hooks, load scripts, and test harness.
- Redwood (customer success): Monica Patel — onboarding, evaluation coordination, artifact collection.
- StellarLex (product): Juan Ramirez — evaluation labels, acceptance sign-off, and internal stakeholder coordination.
- StellarLex (SRE): Priya Shah — joint runbook for simulated failure tests and capacity coordination.

Instrumentations & metrics we will collect (Ben to implement)
- Per-request latency histogram (p50/p90/p95/p99), and token-level timing where possible.
- KV cache hit ratio and size distribution.
- GPU utilization, memory pressure, and batching statistics.
- Cost estimation broken down by model variant and quantization path.

Milestones & timeline (target)
- Week 0 (this week): exchange workload files and access credentials; confirm test dates.
- Week 1: smoke tests + latency tuning (canary run).
- Week 3: scale/throughput test.
- Week 4: blind quality evaluation and result review.
- Week 6: acceptance run + postmortem and next-steps decision (pilot/production).

Immediate asks for StellarLex
- Please share the final labeled evaluation set (or access path) and a short priority list of failure modes you care about.
- Confirm whether the unit-cost target above is acceptable (we set $0.0009 as a conservative starting point).

Attachments: evaluation_workload.csv (recommended test cases + traffic mix).

Thanks — I'll schedule the first technical sync for Friday afternoon and include Ben and Monica.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference for engineering teams
From: Juan Ramirez <juan@stellarlex.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@stellarlex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder handshake: evaluation metrics, ops ownership, and cost limits

Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our discussion. A couple notes / small asks before we lock:  

1) Cost: we appreciate the $0.0009 target, but would you be open to a dual-tier acceptance? If we hit 0.0009 in steady-state that's ideal; for the first two weeks (tuning & canary) we can accept up to $0.0012 while you and Ben tune batching/quantization.

2) Canary cadence: we'd like a short canary in Week 1 (48-hour window) to validate latency under real traffic; if that can pass we'll greenlight the Week 3 full-scale run. Can Ben also include a simple tail-latency report for the canary (p99 + count of >500ms events)?

3) Labels: I'll share a secure link to the labeled evaluation set by EOD Wednesday. There are ~1.6k labeled cases prioritized by severity.

Attachment: stellarlex_questionnaire.pdf — a short security questionnaire our procurement needs to start. Priya will coordinate.

On the cost dual-tier, happy to agree if Redwood documents the tuning steps and expected plan to reach the steady-state target.

Regards,
Juan
Product Lead, StellarLex
juan@stellarlex.com

Looping in the technical plan from our side — quick internal note before the Friday sync.

Proposed telemetry additions (implementation owners in parens)
- Emit per-model-variant token counts to the cost estimator (Ben).
- Add KV cache expvar: hit/miss + windowed TTL distribution (Infra).
- Export batch composition stats (tokens per batch, requests per batch) from the serving runtime (Ben).
- Tail-latency sampler (p99 over 1m windows) forwarded to the dashboard (Monica).

Runbook for Week 1 canary (first-pass)
- Day 1: smoke — verify endpoints, baseline latency, and error rates at low qps.
- Day 2: 48-hour canary at 10–20% of expected traffic (monitor p95/p99 and errors).
- If tail events > 0.1% above baseline, pause and snapshot traces for postmortem.

Owners & resource ask
- Ben: infra + load harness (ETA: Wed end-of-day for initial scripts).
- Monica: will coordinate dataset ingestion and Drive link for labels (ETA: Thu).
- Vivek: please confirm procurement contact for security questionnaire so we can expedite the paperwork.

Notes on cost path to 0.0009/token
- Expect iterative improvements: batching and KV cache tuning (week 1–3), plus quantized single-node variants in week 3.
- We'll provide a cost projection per milestone; initial run will likely be higher (Juan's dual-tier accepted).

Links: hubspot deal (https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deals/1745) and shared folder (https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2b3C/stellerlex-poc).

—
Ben Carter

Thanks team — summary and confirmation of next steps below. I've attached a short MOU to formalize the PoC scope/expectations; please review and return signed if acceptable (MOU-stellarlex.docx attached).

Confirmed items
- Dual-tier cost acceptance: initial tuning window allowable up to $0.0012/token, with a commitment from Redwood to reach <= $0.0009/token by Week 3 via batching/quantization and report the intermediate projections.
- Week 1: Friday technical sync at 3pm PT (invite sent) — Ben will demo the smoke tests plan.
- Week 1 canary: 48-hour window (Monitored p95/p99 + tail events).
- Week 3: full-scale throughput test target 200 QPS.
- Week 4: blind quality evaluation with your labels (Juan to provide link).

Immediate asks for StellarLex (action items)
- Sign and return the attached MOU or send suggested edits.
- Provide the labeled set link (Juan) and SRE contact (Priya added).

Redwood actions (action items)
- Ben: deliver load harness and telemetry changes; tentatively available EOD Wed.
- Monica: ingest labels and set up the evaluation dashboard.
- Vivek: follow up on procurement questionnaire and escalate if SOC2 evidence is requested.

If there are no objections, we'll treat this as the working plan and proceed. Happy to adjust after the Friday sync.

—
